narrative.intro: This ranking shows federal contract obligations by NAICS for FY2026 to date, with a total of $437B in obligations. Direct Health and Medical Insurance Carriers lead the list with $42.5B in obligations, followed by Commercial and Institutional Building Construction at $41.5B and Aircraft Manufacturing at $36B. Engineering Services and Facilities Support Services round out the upper tier with $34.2B and $32.4B respectively. Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences accounted for $30.6B in obligations, while Guided Missile and Space Vehicle Manufacturing totaled $27.9B. Ship Building and Repairing, Computer Systems Design Services, and Other Computer Related Services recorded $23.1B, $21.3B, and $15.4B respectively. These figures are fiscal-year-to-date obligations. The list highlights defense-heavy manufacturing and technical services alongside healthcare administration and construction as the largest NAICS markets for federal contracting so far in FY2026 to date.

sections.heading: Which industries received the largest federal obligations in FY2026 to date?
sections.body: Direct Health and Medical Insurance Carriers received $42.5B in obligations. Commercial and Institutional Building Construction received $41.5B, and Aircraft Manufacturing received $36B. Engineering Services received $34.2B, and Facilities Support Services received $32.4B.

sections.heading: How concentrated are federal obligations across NAICS markets?
sections.body: The top ten NAICS markets together represent a sizeable portion of the $437B total obligations. Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences received $30.6B, Guided Missile and Space Vehicle Manufacturing received $27.9B, and Ship Building and Repairing received $23.1B.

faq.q: What are the biggest federal contracting industries?
faq.a: The biggest federal contracting industries are Direct Health and Medical Insurance Carriers, Commercial and Institutional Building Construction, and Aircraft Manufacturing. Direct Health and Medical Insurance Carriers received $42.5B in obligations. Commercial and Institutional Building Construction received $41.5B in obligations, and Aircraft Manufacturing received $36B in obligations. Other large industries include Engineering Services at $34.2B, Facilities Support Services at $32.4B, and Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences at $30.6B.
